transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It’s, um, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you for fitting me in. 

I, well... I hope I'm not wasting your time. I'm probably just overthinking things, to be honest. But I came in because... for a while now, I’ve been kind of convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are... well, quietly tracking which clients I meet with. 

I know exactly how that sounds, I really do. But it’s just... it feels like they’re sending me little signals? Like through the invitations I get, or the specific topics at panels, or even who happens to sit near me at events. I keep trying to tell myself it could just be a coincidence. I mean, it probably is, right? But I just... I can’t really let it go, no matter how hard I try to brush it off. 

Is... is that the kind of thing I should be bringing up here? I just wanted to make sure I'm explaining things okay.
When this thought comes up, does it feel like an unwanted idea that you recognize might not be true, or does it feel like something you’re certain is really happening?

That is a really good question, doctor. Um... I guess I really *want* it to just be an unwanted idea. Like I was saying a second ago, I try so hard to tell myself it could just be a coincidence. I really want to be rational about it, because I know how it sounds to a professional like you. 

But... when I'm actually in it, you know? When I'm looking at the panel topics or seeing exactly who they seated me next to... it feels incredibly real. I feel certain it's happening. Even when I try to logic my way out of it, I just... I can't really let it go. It just sticks with me. 

Is... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering what you were asking.
About how long have you been having this sense that people are tracking you?

Um, let me think... I'd say it's been about two months? Give or take. 

The whole thing with, you know, feeling like they're tracking my client meetings and sending those signals... it really only started a couple of months ago. It hasn't been going on forever or anything like that. I honestly kept hoping it would just blow over, so I didn't want to make a big fuss and bother anyone with it right away. 

I hope I didn't wait too long to come in and talk to you about it. Does... does two months make sense for something like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a helpful timeline.
Have you heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I haven't heard any voices or... or seen anything that isn't really there. 

I know that's probably a standard question you have to ask, and I totally understand why, but I promise I haven't experienced anything like that. It's really just the... the stuff I mentioned about the panels and the signals. 

Um... that's a good sign, right? That I'm not seeing things or hearing voices? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay, and I hope it helps that I don't have anything like that going on.
Have other people told you lately that your speech or your thoughts seem jumbled or hard to follow?

Um, no... no one has said anything like that to me. I think I'm pretty careful about how I communicate, especially at work with my clients. I try to make sure I'm always clear and professional. 

I mean, I might get a little flustered sometimes, like anyone else, but no one has ever told me I'm hard to understand or that my thoughts are jumbled. I try really hard to keep everything organized when I speak. 

Does... does my speech sound okay to you right now? I hope I'm making sense and being easy to follow. I'd hate to be confusing you.
Right now, do you believe for sure that these people are tracking you?

Um, well... I mean, "for sure" is a strong way to put it, I guess. But... yes, I do believe it's happening. 

I know it sounds a little out there, and I really try to tell myself that it's all just a big coincidence. Like, maybe the panel topics or the invitations or who sits next to me at these events in the arts and finance circles... maybe it's all just random, you know? I really do try to rationalize it that way because I don't want to be the kind of person who jumps to crazy conclusions. 

But... even when I try to brush it off, I just can't seem to let it go. It really feels like they are quietly tracking who I'm meeting with and sending me these little signals. I wouldn't have come in to see you if it wasn't bothering me so much. 

I know that probably sounds a bit strange... I hope you don't think less of me for feeling this way. It's just hard to ignore when it keeps happening. Does that make sense? I'm trying to be as honest as I can about it.
Since this started, have you had a noticeable drop in how well you’re managing at work or in your day-to-day life?

Um... well, I'm definitely still working. I want to make sure you know that. I haven't just stopped or given up or anything like that. I take my career very seriously.

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... my practice has gotten a little smaller lately. I'm honestly a bit embarrassed to admit that, because I've always prided myself on being a really attentive advisor. It's just that, with everything going on, I've been avoiding some of those public panels... just to be safe, you know? 

And because I'm so preoccupied with trying to figure out who's there and what they're doing, I've... well, I've missed a few follow-up calls. I'm just having a little trouble keeping up the exact same level of client contact that I used to manage. 

I really am trying my best to stay on top of everything, though. I hope that doesn't make me sound unprofessional or like I'm falling apart. It's normal to struggle just a little bit at work when you're dealing with a stressful situation like this, isn't it? I just hope I'm handling it okay overall.
Has this belief that people are tracking you lasted for three months or more?

Um, no, definitely not three months. I wouldn't let it go on that long without saying something. I think... well, it's been about two months, roughly. Just the last couple of months is when I really started noticing the... the tracking of my client meetings and those signals I mentioned. 

I really wanted to make sure I talked to someone before it got out of hand. I'm trying to be really proactive about everything, you know? I didn't want to just ignore it and let it affect my work more than it has. So, just about two months. That means we caught it pretty early, right? I hope that makes it a little easier for us to figure out.
Did this belief start very suddenly, over a day or two?

Um, no... I don't think it was just overnight. It wasn't like I woke up one morning and suddenly thought, "Oh, they're tracking me." I really want to be clear about that, because I know how that might sound. 

It was more... gradual, I guess? Like, I just started noticing little things here and there over a few weeks. The panel topics, the seating arrangements... it just sort of built up slowly until I couldn't ignore it anymore. 

I feel like that's a pretty normal way to realize something's wrong, isn't it? Just putting the pieces together over time. I hope that makes sense... I'm really trying not to sound like someone who just snaps and jumps to wild conclusions.
Since this started, have you found yourself losing motivation to do everyday things?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I've completely lost motivation. I mean, I'm still doing what I need to do, mostly. I still get my work done... just, you know, maybe in smaller pieces than before. I really want to make sure you know I'm not just lying in bed all day or anything like that. 

But I guess... if I'm being totally honest... I just don't have that same spark I used to have. It's a little embarrassing to admit, but I've been leaving some of my client follow-ups just sitting there for a bit. And outside of work... I've sort of been skipping my usual jazz nights, and I haven't been going to pickup basketball either. And the weird thing is, I don't even really feel bad about missing them. It's just... I don't know, it just feels like so much effort right now. 

Even when my friends ask what's going on, I just kind of give them really short answers. Talking just feels... heavier than it should, if that makes sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or like I'm not trying. It's just a lot to process right now, and I think it's normal to pull back a little bit when you're stressed, right? I'm sure I'll get that energy back once we get this all sorted out.
Have people lately commented that you seem emotionally flat or less expressive than usual?

Um, no, no one's really said anything like that. I mean, I try to keep a smile on, especially with my clients. You kind of have to in my line of work, right? You want people to feel confident in you. 

I guess maybe I've been a little quieter, like I mentioned with my friends, but I wouldn't say I'm... flat. I'm still me! I still laugh when things are funny and all that. I just... maybe I'm just a little more focused right now, with everything going on. That's a pretty normal reaction to stress, don't you think? Just being a bit more reserved? I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around staring blankly at the wall or anything. I'm definitely still engaged... just, you know, maybe a little more low-key for the time being.
Before these last two months, had you long been someone who tended to be unusually suspicious of other people’s motives?

Um, no, definitely not. I really want to make sure you know that this isn't how I usually am. Before the last couple of months, I've actually always been a pretty trusting guy. 

I mean, in my line of work, you really have to build strong relationships, right? You can't be a good financial advisor if you're always second-guessing your clients or your colleagues. I've always prided myself on being easy to get along with and seeing the best in people. 

So, no, I wasn't ever someone who was unusually suspicious of anyone's motives before all this. I hope that shows that I'm normally a very reasonable person... I really don't want you to think I've just been walking around distrusting everyone my whole life. That's a good sign, isn't it? That this is just a recent thing and not my normal personality?
Have you had the experience that your thoughts were being inserted into your mind by someone else?

Oh, um... no. No, I haven't experienced anything like that. That sounds... really intense, actually. 

My thoughts are definitely my own. I mean, sure, sometimes I get a little overwhelmed or my mind races a bit when I'm stressed about work or... or just trying to figure out what's going on lately. But I always know it's just me thinking. Nobody is putting thoughts in my head or anything like that. 

I'm still very grounded in that way, you know? I really want to be clear that I'm not losing touch with reality like that. That's a good thing, right? That I'm still completely in control of my own mind? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's happening.
During these last two months, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed? Um... no, definitely not. I wouldn't use that word at all. 

I mean, sure, things have been a bit stressful lately, but I'm certainly not feeling sad or down all day. I still get up, go to work, take care of my clients... I'm still functioning perfectly fine. I just want to make sure you don't think I'm, you know, giving up or just lying in bed all day or anything like that. I'm really not. 

I'm just dealing with some pressure, which I think is pretty understandable. It's totally normal to feel a little stressed without actually being depressed, right? I hope that shows I'm still handling things pretty well overall.
For how much of these last two months have you been having this belief that people are tracking you?

Um, well, it's... it's been about two months, I guess. Since it started. 

But I want to be clear, it's not like it's taking over my whole life or anything. It's just... I've noticed things, you know? Like people keeping tabs on my client meetings, or... or maybe sending little signals. But I'm still doing my job, I'm still taking care of my clients. I just have to be a little more observant lately, that's all. 

It's been about two months of just... noticing these things. That's not too long, is it? I mean, anyone in my position might pick up on things if they were really paying attention, right? I just want to make sure you know I'm still handling everything professionally.
For at least one full month during this time, have these beliefs been present continuously?

Continuously? Um, no... no, definitely not. It hasn't been like a 24/7 thing for a whole month straight or anything like that. 

I mean, that sounds really exhausting, honestly. It's more just... passing thoughts, you know? Like, I'll be reviewing a portfolio or heading into the office, and I'll just notice something a little off. But then I just brush it off and get right back to work. 

I wouldn't be able to manage my clients' accounts if I was distracted by that all day, every day. So it really just comes and goes. That's a lot better, right? That I'm able to just put it aside and stay focused on my job?
Have the people close to you noticed that your facial expressions or tone of voice seem less expressive than usual lately?

Um... my friends? I guess... maybe they've mentioned I seem a little quiet or distant lately. But it's not like I'm totally blank or a robot or anything, I promise. 

I just... I guess I don't have the exact same spark right now. I'm still getting my work done, of course! Just... maybe in pieces. Like, I might leave some routine client follow-ups sitting a little longer than usual. And I've skipped a few of my usual jazz nights and pickup basketball games. The weird part is I don't really feel much about missing them. 

So when my friends ask what's going on, I guess I do give pretty short answers. It's just that talking feels like a lot more effort than it should right now. But I'm still keeping things together and doing my job. That just sounds like regular burnout, right? I hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm doing poorly, because I'm really trying my best to stay on top of things.
Before these last two months, had you already been less motivated or less emotionally expressive for a long time?

Um... well, I guess it depends on what you mean by a long time. I definitely wouldn't say I've been completely unmotivated or anything negative like that! I've always cared about my clients. 

But, um... I suppose if I really think about it, these... these changes, like being a little quieter or pacing myself more... they have been building for a while. Probably since this arts nonprofit recognition I got. That was, um, a little over two years ago. 

But it's not like I just gave up on everything two years ago, I promise! It's just been a really slow, gradual thing. You know, you achieve something nice, and then you just naturally kind of settle down and get a bit more serious, right? That's a pretty normal professional adjustment to make, isn't it? I just want to make sure you know I haven't been just sitting around doing nothing all that time. I've still been working hard.
Compared with a couple of years ago, has your ability to function at work and socially clearly declined?

Declined? Um... I don't know if I'd use the word declined. That sounds a little severe, doesn't it? I mean, I am absolutely still working. I really want to make sure you know that I haven't just stopped trying. 

But, um... I guess if I look at the numbers, my practice has gotten a little smaller. I just... well, like I mentioned before, I've missed some follow-ups, and I've been avoiding some of the public financial panels I used to speak on. It's just been a little harder lately to keep up the exact same level of constant client contact that I used to manage. 

But I'm still taking care of my core clients! I'm just focusing on quality over quantity right now. That's a pretty normal way to restructure a business as you get older, right? I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm failing at my career, because I promise I'm still putting in the effort.
